claims.text: The city's update on its Sanitation and Code Compliance AI camera system was addressed to the Quality of Life, Arts, and Culture Committee.
claims.quote: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System Quality of Life, Arts, and Culture Committee
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The briefing deck is dated October 19th, 2026.
claims.quote: Code Compliance Services October 19, 2026
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: City Detect is a computer vision tool that flags possible exterior property and right-of-way conditions for trained staff to review.
claims.quote: City Detect is a computer vision tool used to identify potential exterior property and right-of-way conditions for review by trained staff.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city states that a computer vision observation is not a confirmed Code violation and that city staff make that call.
claims.quote: A computer vision observation is not a confirmed Code violation. City staff make that determination.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The cameras ride on 50 Sanitation brush collection vehicles that already travel Dallas neighborhoods on routine service.
claims.quote: Cameras are mounted on 50 Sanitation brush collection vehicles that already travel Dallas neighborhoods during routine service.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: Conditions are observed along existing routes. The city says no separate Code Compliance patrol routes are created.
claims.quote: Exterior conditions are observed along existing routes. No separate Code Compliance patrol routes are created.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck lists identifying possible exterior conditions as one thing the technology does.
claims.quote: Identifies potential exterior conditions
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck also says the technology helps staff decide which areas to review first.
claims.quote: Helps staff prioritize areas for review
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck says the technology does not decide on its own that a Code violation exists.
claims.quote: Determine by itself that a Code violation exists
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck says the technology does not replace the judgment of a Code Officer.
claims.quote: Replace Code Officer judgment
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck says the technology does not automatically open formal enforcement based only on a computer vision observation.
claims.quote: Automatically create formal enforcement solely from a computer vision observation
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: According to the city's privacy slide, faces and license plates are blurred inside the system.
claims.quote: Faces and license plates are blurred within the system.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck says staff review every computer generated observation before Code Compliance takes any action.
claims.quote: Computer-generated observations are subject to staff review before Code Compliance action.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck says City staff decide the right response to a detection and the technology does not decide it automatically.
claims.quote: The appropriate response is determined by City Staff-not automatically by technology.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: Under the previous approach, the first letter a resident got was a formal notice of violation and the first step toward a citation.
claims.quote: The first letter a resident received was a formal notice of violation, the first step toward a citation if not addressed.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: Under the current approach, a first courtesy letter is an educational reminder. It sits outside the citation process and sets no deadline.
claims.quote: When a courtesy notice is used, the first letter received is an educational notice: a friendly reminder that is not part of the citation process and sets no deadline.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city says a courtesy notice alone never opens a formal enforcement case.
claims.quote: No formal enforcement case is opened solely due to the courtesy notice.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: In a prioritized inspection, a trained Code Officer first reviews the observation and decides whether it calls for a field inspection.
claims.quote: A trained Code Officer reviews the observation and determines whether the condition warrants a field inspection.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: Next, a Code Inspector does an on-site inspection to find out whether a violation exists.
claims.quote: A Code Inspector conducts an on-site inspection to determine whether a violation exists.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city calls computer vision observations potential conditions for review that should not be read as confirmed violations or enforcement actions.
claims.quote: Computer vision observations represent potential conditions identified for review and should not be interpreted as confirmed violations or enforcement actions.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: A slide on proactive neighborhood awareness reads 32% proactive and 68% reactive. The slide does not say what those shares are measured across.
claims.quote: 32% Proactive | 68% Reactive
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city's results table reports 5,318 observations reviewed to date.
claims.quote: citations generated. Observations Reviewed 5,318
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The results table reports 2,928 courtesy notices.
claims.quote: Observations Reviewed 5,318 Courtesy Notices 2,928
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The results table reports 473 field inspections.
claims.quote: Courtesy Notices 2,928 Field Inspections 473
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The results table reports 374 voluntary corrections.
claims.quote: Field Inspections 473 Voluntary Corrections 374
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The results table reports 34 direct abatements.
claims.quote: Voluntary Corrections 374 Direct Abatements 34
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The results table lists 101 under formal enforcement.
claims.quote: Direct Abatements 34 Formal Enforcement 101
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city says success is measured by better neighborhood conditions and service delivery rather than by the number of citations generated.
claims.quote: Success is measured by improved neighborhood conditions and effective service delivery—not by the number of citations generated.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: Among its next steps, the city plans to keep calibrating detection accuracy and its staff validation processes.
claims.quote: Continue calibrating detection accuracy and staff validation processes.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The city also plans to set performance measures for accuracy, response, voluntary compliance, resource use and neighborhood outcomes.
claims.quote: Establish performance measures around accuracy, response, voluntary compliance, resource utilization and neighborhood outcomes.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The Brush and Bulky program offers monthly pickup of up to 10 cubic yards, with a once annual 20 yd3 exception.
claims.quote: The Brush and Bulky Waste Collection Program provides customers with monthly pick-up of up to 10 cubic yards (once annual 20 yd3 exception)
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: The deck closes by saying technology identifies potential conditions and people make the decisions.
claims.quote: Technology identifies potential conditions. People make the decisions.
claims.document: Update on the Sanitation and Code Compliance AI Camera System

claims.text: An earlier briefing to the Finance Committee on the AI-powered camera technology is dated December 9th, 2025.
claims.quote: AI-Powered Camera Technology Finance Committee Date: 12/9/2025
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The December briefing proposed putting 100 AI-enabled cameras on Sanitation brush trucks.
claims.quote: Implement 100 AI-enabled cameras on Sanitation brush trucks
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The December briefing describes a three-year contract estimated at $2,556,000, subject to annual City Council appropriations.
claims.quote: This is a three-year contract for an estimated amount of $2,556,000, subject to annual City Council appropriations.
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The briefing puts the contract cost at $852,000 per year, covering 100 cameras plus installation, data services, maintenance and replacement support.
claims.quote: The contract cost is $852,000 per year, which includes 100 cameras and all associated technology, installation, data services, maintenance, warranty, and replacement support.
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The briefing says the city may end the contract at any time on 10 days written notice without penalty.
claims.quote: The City may terminate the contract with 10 days’ written notice at any time, without penalty.
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The December briefing said there is a human in the loop for all actions.
claims.quote: There is a human in the loop for all actions
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: According to the December briefing, the cameras automatically blur license plate numbers and faces.
claims.quote: Automated blurring of personal information (license plate numbers and faces)
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: The December briefing said the City Council would consider the item on December 10th, 2025.
claims.quote: This item will be considered by the City Council on December 10, 2025
claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology

claims.text: A city memo answering budget listening session questions is dated April 10th, 2026.
claims.quote: DATE April 10, 2026 CITY OF DALLAS
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: The memo says the AI-enabled cameras are budgeted at $853,000 in the Department of Sanitation operating budget.
claims.quote: The artificial intelligence (AI) -enabled cameras are budgeted at $853,000 within the Department of Sanitation’s operating budget.
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: The memo says Sanitation is an enterprise fund department paid for through user fees rather than the General Fund.
claims.quote: Sanitation is an enterprise fund department, meaning its services are funded through user fees rather than General Fund.
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: The memo says cameras will be installed on 50 brush and bulky waste trucks, two per vehicle.
claims.quote: Cameras will be installed on 50 brush and bulky waste trucks (two per vehicle)
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: The memo says the technology will issue no automatic citations and Code Compliance staff will verify every potential violation before acting.
claims.quote: No automatic citations will be issued as a result of this technology. All potential violations will be reviewed and verified by Code Compliance staff before any action is taken.
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: The memo says the city will keep ownership and control of all data the system collects.
claims.quote: The City will retain ownership and control of all data collected through this system.
claims.document: Follow-up to the City Council Listening Sessions in Advance of FY 2026-27 Budget Development

claims.text: FOX 4 reported that a city memo said the cameras found 3,700 violations that led to notices and 57 citations at 34 properties.
claims.quote: A recent city memo says the cameras have found 3,700 violations that led to notices and 57 citations handed out to 34 different properties.
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: FOX 4 reported the memo says citations are issued only after a code officer inspects the property in person and notifies the owner.
claims.quote: The memo also states citations are only issued after a code officer inspects the property in-person and provides notice to the owner.
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: FOX 4 attributed its figures to a September 8th memo from the City of Dallas. That memo was not fetched for this record.
claims.quote: A September 8 memo from the City of Dallas detailed the findings and costs of AI-powered cameras
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: FOX 4 reported the memo says the cameras scanned 10,000 properties.
claims.quote: According to the memo, the cameras have scanned 10,000 properties and have resulted in 3,700 violations, resulting in notices from the city.
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: FOX 4 published its report on September 18th, 2026.
claims.quote: September 18, 2026 4:46 PM CDT
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

rejected.finding: The does-not-do line about tracking individuals
rejected.reason: The printed line is two words, under the quote minimum, and no other sentence in the four sources says it. Not carried.

rejected.finding: The 3,700, 57 and 34 figures as the city's own
rejected.reason: They exist only in FOX 4's account of a September 8th memo that was not fetched. Carried only as FOX 4's reporting (c47, c49, c50).

rejected.finding: FOX 4 headline figure of almost 4,000 notices
rejected.reason: The headline rounds. The body says 3,700.

rejected.finding: What the 32% proactive and 68% reactive split measures
rejected.reason: The slide gives no population or period. Any denominator would be invented.

rejected.finding: That the council approved the contract on December 10th, 2025
rejected.reason: The December briefing says only that the item will be considered on that date. No source records the vote.

rejected.finding: Any accuracy, false positive or error rate for the detections
rejected.reason: None is published. The October 19th briefing lists calibrating accuracy and setting accuracy measures as next steps (c29, c30).

rejected.finding: NBC 5's October reporting on the blight score label
rejected.reason: nbcdfw.com is refused by the crawl boundary, so nothing from it is carried.
